questions.prompt: A policy has liability limits of 25/50/25 (thousands). Luis causes a crash that injures one person with $40,000 of medical bills. How much might Luis owe himself?
questions.intro: Liability coverage pays for injuries and damage you cause to others. Limits like 25/50/25 mean $25,000 per injured person, $50,000 for all injuries in one crash, and $25,000 for property damage. The driver can owe anything above the limits.

misconceptions.B: Subtracts the bill from the $50,000 per-accident limit

questions.prompt: Which coverage pays to fix Luis's own car after he hits a pole?

choices.text: Collision
Liability, which pays for damage to others
Comprehensive, which covers theft, fire, and hail
Uninsured motorist, for crashes with uninsured drivers

questions.intro: Collision pays for damage to your car from a crash, minus the deductible. Comprehensive covers non-crash damage (theft, fire, storms, hitting a deer).
questions.feedback: Collision covers your car in a crash you cause.

questions.prompt: New Jersey is a "no-fault" state. Which coverage pays the medical bills of Luis and his passengers after a crash, regardless of fault?

choices.text: Collision, which pays to fix his own car
Personal injury protection (PIP)
Liability, which pays for harm he causes to others

questions.intro: Auto coverages: liability pays for harm you cause to others; collision repairs your car after a crash; personal injury protection (PIP), required in no-fault states such as New Jersey, pays your own medical costs no matter who caused the crash.
questions.feedback: PIP pays medical bills for you and your passengers in no-fault states.

questions.prompt: Luis's car is worth $2,000. Collision coverage costs $600 a year with a $500 deductible. What is the most collision would pay in a total loss?
questions.intro: Collision pays up to the car's actual cash value minus the deductible. On an older car, it can cost close to what it could ever pay.

questions.prompt: Raising the deductible from $500 to $1,000 lowers Luis's premium by $150 a year. How many claim-free years until the savings cover the extra $500 risk?

choices.text: About 0.3 years
About 3.3 years
About 6.7 years
About 1.5 years

questions.intro: A higher deductible lowers the premium. Break-even years = extra deductible ÷ yearly savings.

misconceptions.A: Divides savings by the extra deductible
